concepts.def: Inner struggle against sin to be a better Muslim
Defensive armed struggle to protect Islam
Muslim place of worship and community

walkthroughs.body_html:
Jihad literally means 'striving'.

The Greater Jihad is the inner struggle to follow Allah — controlling anger, greed, laziness — and the most important kind.

The Lesser Jihad is armed struggle, allowed only in self-defence with strict rules (no harming civilians, women, children, trees or crops).

Terrorism violates these rules and is condemned by mainstream Muslim scholars.

Halal = permitted. Includes meat slaughtered Islamically with Allah's name pronounced.

Haram = forbidden. Includes pork, alcohol, gambling, riba (interest on loans) and zina (sex outside marriage).

Qur'an 2:173 lists key forbidden foods.

The Ummah — global Muslim community — has around 1.8 billion members, the world's second-largest religion.

In the UK, around 4 million Muslims live (2021 Census). UK mosques play roles in prayer, education, charity and community.

Challenges include Islamophobia, balancing modern life with religious duties, and representing Islam against extremist distortions.

mcqs.q: Which Jihad is considered greater — and most important — by Muslim scholars?
What does the term jihad mean in Islam?
options: Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Struggle or striving — the greater jihad is the internal spiritual struggle against sin; the lesser jihad refers to defensive military struggle under strict conditions.

mcqs.q: What are the main Christian theories of atonement?
options: The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.
All Christians believe Jesus died only to pay God back for sin.

Penal substitution (Christ bore the punishment for sin), Christus Victor (Christ defeated evil powers through the cross), ransom theory (Christ paid a price to free humanity), and moral exemplar (Christ's death inspires love). Different traditions emphasise different theories.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.
Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
